title: SL Green Agrees to Sell 43% Stake in 1515 Broadway in Manhattan to Allianz
summary: SL Green Realty Corp. has agreed to sell a 43% stake in the 1.86 million square foot Times Square office tower at 1515 Broadway to Allianz Real Estate. This deal values the tower, which houses Viacom Inc. headquarters and the Minskoff Theater, at $1.95 billion. Allianz Group's real-estate investment division, based in Germany, is the purchaser of the stake.

title: Inside the Wal-Mart vs. Amazon Battle Over Black Friday
summary: This article examines the Black Friday battle between Wal-Mart and Amazon, highlighting the ongoing shift from in-store to online holiday shopping. While online sales surged, some consumers still opted for in-person deals, demonstrating the new tactics both retailers are employing. The report notes a decline in traditional store visits alongside a significant increase in online purchases during the Thanksgiving and Black Friday period.

title: Is There Time for QVC in the Age of Amazon?
summary: QVC Inc. is facing new challenges to its business model, with U.S. sales falling 6% in its third quarter, marking the first drop in seven years. This decline is attributed to competition from traditional and online retailers, including Amazon, and has negatively impacted the company's stock value. The article questions QVC's ability to compete in the current e-commerce landscape.

title: What You Need to Know About GRAIL
summary: Grail Bio, launched by Illumina in 2016, aims to develop a blood test for early detection of all cancer types, leveraging Illumina's gene sequencing technology. The company, backed by prominent investors like Jeff Bezos and Bill Gates, plans clinical trials for a pan-cancer screening test and a single-cancer test in 2017, with potential market availability for the pan-cancer test by 2019. It faces competition from other companies developing liquid biopsy tests for cancer detection.

title: CES 2017: Amazon Echo-Style Voice Control Is Coming to More Appliances
summary: At CES 2017, Whirlpool announced that its new home appliances will be compatible with Amazon's Alexa voice assistant, allowing users to control tasks like laundry and oven settings with voice commands. This partnership signifies Amazon's strategy to integrate Alexa deeper into the smart home ecosystem, facing competition from other tech giants like Apple and Samsung who are also developing their own voice-controlled platforms.

title: Macy's to close 68 stores, 4 in Philadelphia area
summary: Macy's announced plans to eliminate over 10,000 jobs and close 68 stores, including four in the Philadelphia area, after a disappointing holiday shopping season. The department store chain lowered its full-year earnings forecast, citing changing consumer behavior and increased online shopping as primary reasons for declining sales. The closures are part of a larger plan to restructure the business and save an estimated $550 million annually, with share prices falling over 8% in after-hours trading.

title: SanDisk: USB drive with SSD performance
summary: Western Digital Corporation announced the 256GB SanDisk Extreme PRO USB 3.1 Solid State Flash Drive at CES 2017, touting SSD-like performance in a portable USB form factor. This drive offers read speeds up to 420MB/s and write speeds up to 380MB/s, making it ideal for transferring large files like 4K movies quickly, and includes SanDisk SecureAccess software for file encryption. It's set to be available in late January 2017 for $179.99.

title: Is There Time for QVC in the Age of Amazon?
summary: QVC is experiencing its first decline in U.S. sales in seven years, raising questions about its ability to compete against e-commerce giants like Amazon. The home-shopping channel's business model, which relies on impulsive TV purchases, is showing cracks, affecting the value of QVC Group shares. Executives have warned that the sales declines continued into the crucial holiday quarter.

title: Amazon to surpass 1 GW of clean energy capacity. Is it enough?
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is set to significantly expand its renewable energy capacity, nearing 1 GW of wind and solar power in 2017, positioning itself as a major player in clean computing infrastructure. Despite these substantial investments, the company faces criticism for a lack of transparency regarding its overall energy consumption and carbon footprint compared to its competitors. Amazon is focused on broadening renewable energy adoption, particularly in regions where it has been slower to catch on, and is actively participating in clean energy policy debates.

title: Gildan wins American Apparel auction with $88M bid
summary: Gildan Activewear Inc. won the auction for American Apparel's brand and certain assets with a cash bid of $88 million, excluding its 110 stores. This acquisition allows Gildan to integrate the brand into its printwear business and leverage its distribution networks, capping off a tumultuous period for American Apparel. The transaction is pending Delaware bankruptcy court approval.

title: American Apparel Acquired by Gildan Activewear for $88 Million
summary: Bankrupt L.A.-based retailer American Apparel was acquired by Canadian brand Gildan Activewear for $88 million following a court-supervised auction. The acquisition, which still needs bankruptcy court approval, includes the American Apparel brand and certain assets but does not include its retail stores. Gildan plans to leverage its extensive printwear distribution networks to grow American Apparel sales.

title: American Apparel bankruptcy leaves retail future in doubt, Gildan says not obligated to keep employees
summary: Canadian T-shirt and underwear maker Gildan Activewear has acquired American Apparel's intellectual property and other assets for US$88 million after the latter's bankruptcy auction, without committing to keep American Apparel's employees or stores. This marks American Apparel's second bankruptcy in 13 months, prompting concerns about the future of its Los Angeles garment workers and the brand itself. Founder Dov Charney expressed disappointment, blaming "reckless Wall Street behavior" for the company's downfall, which involved 4,700 employees and 110 stores prior to its second bankruptcy filing.

summary: The article examines how investors react when companies transition to a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) business model, using Adobe Inc. as a primary example. title: Worldwide IT spending forecast to grow 2.7% in 2017: Gartner
summary: Worldwide IT spending is projected to reach US$3.5 trillion in 2017, a 2.7% increase from 2016, according to Gartner. This growth rate is lower than earlier projections due to political uncertainty causing enterprises to delay investments. Despite this, some sectors like cloud computing platforms are seeing aggressive build-outs, leading to higher projected growth.

title: How to Stop the Amazon Echo From Buying Stuff
summary: This article provides a guide on how to prevent the Amazon Echo from making unintended purchases through voice commands. It details steps to disable voice purchasing entirely or set up a confirmation code using the Amazon Alexa app, following an incident where a child reportedly ordered a dollhouse. The instructions apply to all Alexa-compatible devices, ensuring users can control accidental orders.

title: Amazon takes office space in T3 building in North Loop
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has signed a lease for office space in the T3 building in Minneapolis's North Loop, becoming the first major tenant in the new all-timber commercial property. The company plans to house its local technology development office there, eventually employing 100 workers, and will move employees from an existing office at the Fifth Street Towers. T3 is notable for being the first commercial property in the U.S. completely built with engineered wood and is lauded for its superior internet connectivity.

title: Radial challenges Amazon with expanded fulfillment service
summary: Omnichannel commerce operations provider Radial is expanding its fulfillment services to compete with Amazon. The company is rolling out new technologies, services, and partnerships to help mid-market retailers, which often lack the resources to compete with Amazon, improve their consumer experience and profitability. Radial, formed from eBay Enterprise and Innotrac, aims to provide comprehensive order management, payment processing, fulfillment, and analytics services to its clients.

title: Salesforce opens engineering office in Microsoft’s and Amazon’s backyards
summary: Salesforce announced the opening of a new engineering and innovation hub in Bellevue, Washington, significantly expanding its presence in the Seattle area, home to rivals Microsoft and Amazon. The office will primarily focus on its artificial intelligence initiative, Einstein, and plans to double its current 250 employees. This move addresses the challenge of finding engineering talent in the Bay Area and allows Salesforce to establish a foothold near its competitors.

title: Salesforce shows off new office tower in Bellevue
summary: Salesforce.com has opened a new office tower in Bellevue, moving most of its Seattle-area employees into the top three floors of the 929 Office Tower. The company expects to reach 500 employees in the area soon, making this office one of its largest engineering hubs. This move signifies the continued expansion of Silicon Valley tech giants into the Seattle area, joining other major players like Amazon, Microsoft, Facebook, and Google.

title: Service Contract Pricing: Refrigerators, 19 January 2017
summary: This article analyzes service contract pricing for refrigerators, finding that the ratio of protection plan cost to product list price decreases as the refrigerator's price increases. It identifies that pricing varies significantly among retailers and administrators, and while brand doesn't affect service contract prices much, the duration of coverage and the product's price band are key determinants. The analysis also reveals a "floor" and "ceiling" for service contract pricing, driven by repair costs and claim likelihood.

title: Target makes big push into soccer marketing
summary: Target Corp. is making its biggest push into team sports through a multi-pronged soccer marketing partnership. This includes a three-year deal with Major League Soccer, sponsorship of Minnesota United FC with the company's bullseye on jerseys, and becoming the official retailer for U.S. Youth Soccer. The move reflects Target's shift in marketing strategy to focus on growing demographics like Hispanics, families, and millennials, who show strong affinity for soccer.

title: Rick Gomez will become Target's new chief marketer
summary: Target Corp. has promoted Rick Gomez to Chief Marketing Officer, a key role focused on cultivating the retailer's brand image. Gomez, previously a senior vice president, will take over from Jeff Jones and be responsible for driving traffic, sales, and loyalty. He has been instrumental in initiatives like the Gwen Stefani music video and the Lilly Pulitzer collaboration, and will continue efforts to deepen customer research and target diverse demographics.

title: Exclusive | Amazon’s next frontier to conquer? Auto parts
summary: Amazon is reportedly eyeing the $50 billion do-it-yourself after-market auto parts business as its next major sector to dominate. The e-commerce giant has struck deals with large parts manufacturers and is offering same-day delivery in many cities at prices significantly lower than brick-and-mortar competitors like O’Reilly Auto Parts, Advance Auto Parts, and AutoZone. This move is expected to disrupt the traditional auto parts retail market, which has relied on high profit margins and control over suppliers.

title: Kroger to hire 10,000 store employees
summary: Kroger announced plans to hire 10,000 permanent employees across its various store chains, part of a larger trend of U.S. companies expanding hiring. This move comes as traditional retailers face competition from online sellers and despite Kroger's recent struggles with food price deflation and a profit drop in the third quarter. The company previously offered early retirement to nearly 2,000 workers to cut costs.

title: Company launches 'smart'-hearing protection for hunters, civilian shooters
summary: 3M Co. has launched new "smart" hearing protection headsets, the Peltor Sport Electronic Hearing Protector, for hunters and civilian shooters. These devices automatically suppress gun noises while amplifying voices and phone conversations. 3M anticipates expanding its market reach significantly with these products, which are expected to sell for $149.99 and $199.99, and capitalize on the growing U.S. hearing protection market.

title: Swift: Most In-Demand Language for Developers
summary: Upwork's Q4 2016 report on fastest-growing skills identifies Swift as the most in-demand language, even though natural language processing holds the top spot for overall desirable technology. The article attributes Swift's rise to the popularity of Apple products, including the Apple Watch, and notes its growing dominance over Objective-C among Apple developers. It also highlights other top skills like natural language processing, Tableau, Amazon Marketplace, and Stripe, indicating trends in employer demand for freelancers.

title: Ontario International Airport Courts Chinese Versions of FedEx, UPS
summary: Ontario International Airport executives are actively pursuing major Chinese courier companies like SF Express and STO Express to establish the airport as a primary gateway and hub for U.S. and Latin American markets. This aggressive air service development campaign aims to capitalize on bidirectional e-commerce opportunities, drawing parallels to the domestic operations of UPS and FedEx. The initiative also coincided with discussions on the Trump administration's trade policies and their potential impact on local exporters.

title: Tech Companies Fight Trump Immigration Order in Court (Published 2017)
summary: Amazon and Expedia have intensified their opposition to President Trump's immigration order by filing declarations in a federal lawsuit, arguing that the order would negatively impact their businesses and operations. This move represents an escalation of the tech industry's efforts to challenge the executive order, which restricts immigration from several Muslim-majority countries. Other tech companies like Google also saw employee demonstrations against the order.
